design_condition: The orthogonal comb occupies the southern plot between the historic complex and the city, using alternating courtyards and building arms to improve permeability and create differentiated public, semi-private, and intimate outdoor spaces.

positive.statement: The comb structure creates an interesting spatial transition between the historic enclosure and the existing city.
The orthogonal placement facilitates north-south permeability and establishes a hierarchy of external spaces and circulation.
The sequence of built bodies and courtyards successfully reproduces the dimensions of the existing spaces.
The differentiation of public spaces, including more intimate residential areas, is an important quality.
The housing typologies are well studied, and the variation of modules is convincing.
The greenery and paths remain continuous through the enclosure and connect the river with the school garden.
The urban forest positively affects the microclimate and filters emissions from the surrounding road.
The green roof and insulated load-bearing structure are effective choices.

negative.statement: The relationship between the base and upper part of the new volume is unconvincing.
The distribution and accesses are ambiguous, with consequences for the façades.
The different connections between the comb arms and central body create an inconsistency between courtyards.
The distribution system is spatially interesting but rather complicated.
The relevance of opening skylights in the existing roof is questioned.
The relationship with the historical complex is not entirely convincing.
The execution methods require better verification given the complex geometry.
Summer thermal comfort and cooling needs, especially in glazed common areas, must be checked.
The treatment of systems in the existing buildings is less in-depth.
